items.quote: I feel I need to get a divorce for financial reasons as well as my sanity. I don't want to abandon him, but I have to look out for myself.
items.label: protect own sanity and finances

items.quote: When I understood she really wasn't being a jerk but was sick and didn't know, then I knew I was staying.
items.label: understanding illness made me stay

items.quote: For me, I just could not abandon my DH who I loved dearly just because I was afraid.
items.label: love, cannot abandon husband

items.quote: I am so overwhelmed with his bills- left so unintended- and the lack of addressing so many things when he walked out of his job
items.label: overwhelmed by husband's neglected bills

items.quote: I have trouble getting him in the car. He gained alot of weight he is 200 lbs. I have trouble dressing him and getting him in shower.
items.label: physically hard to move and dress him

items.quote: I am very angry about how this has changed my life and often engage him in arguments and yell at him.
items.label: anger and yelling at husband

items.quote: How can I help myself to stop this behavior?
items.label: stop arguing and yelling

items.quote: Our wedding vows are all I need to set my needs aside.
items.label: wedding vows drive care

items.quote: Trying to find the balance between being a partner and a caregiver has been one of my biggest challenges in caring for my DH.
items.label: balancing partner and caregiver roles

items.quote: Just want everyone to be safe
items.label: wants everyone to be safe

items.quote: I’ve been noticing when he drives he’s slowing down at all intersections even if the light is green.
items.label: husband's driving is changing

items.quote: I’m going to ask him to be evaluated at a driving center soon.
items.label: get driving evaluation

items.quote: I'm so heartbroken that this might be a conversation we need to have quickly. I thought we had time.
items.label: driving talk needed sooner than expected

items.quote: I still have to work full time so I have finally come to the place it is better for him and me to do this.
items.label: place husband in memory care

items.quote: I want to make this as easy for him as I can.
items.label: make the move easy for him

items.quote: The lying to him is a hard thing to do since I haven’t lied to him in 45 years….but I will do whatever if it makes this easier for him.
items.label: will do whatever eases it for him

items.quote: Honestly, there is no chance we will be able to pay for any memory care.
items.label: cannot afford memory care

items.quote: how does everyone pay for MC?
items.label: find way to pay for memory care

items.quote: Like you, I still work and arranging care at home is difficult.
items.label: working while arranging care at home

items.quote: I just feel so angry and tired and unsupported all the time.
items.label: angry, tired, unsupported

items.quote: I am constantly tired because, he just got a catheter.
items.label: exhausted by catheter care

items.quote: Struggling to get more hours at a job I just got.
items.label: get more hours at new job

items.quote: I’m struggling with figuring out health insurance for myself and I’m tired.
items.label: figuring out own health insurance

items.quote: After 8 years of dealing with hubby's progressing dementia, and fighting him about taking the 8-15 pills daily, I have started asking about quality of life rather than quantity.
items.label: reduce pills, favor quality of life

items.quote: If I happen to fall asleep, hubby, a type 2 diabetic will sneak ice cream and anything sweet he can find.
items.label: husband sneaks sweets when I sleep

items.quote: They want him to exercise, but I cannot go for walks with him due to my rollator and bad knee from an irrepairable Achille's tendon tear.
items.label: cannot walk with him for exercise

items.quote: We are on free food from local pantries, which results in a high number of carbs which we cannot do much about
items.label: pantry food is high in carbs

items.quote: Most days the aide comes while I am at work, and by evening I realize I honestly do not know how the visit went.
items.label: not knowing how aide visit went

items.quote: I feel guilty double-checking on people, but I feel worse not knowing.
items.label: guilt about checking on aide

items.quote: I also wanted to know they did what needed to be done.
items.label: know aides did the needed care

items.quote: I was worried about counting on an aide coming every day and being reliable.
items.label: worry aide may not be reliable

items.quote: when I was gone for a few hours at a time, she had nothing to hold her accountable, she didn't do anything at all.
items.label: aide did nothing when I was away

items.quote: I pray for patience and compassion and I thank God daily for the ability to care for and about my DH’s feelings as he is struggling with what he’s going through.
items.label: patience and compassion for his feelings

items.quote: I have to be sensitive to slight changes in his mood and to my reactions to things that happen because it’s easy for me to react strongly and hurt his feelings.
items.label: must watch my reactions and his moods

items.quote: I’m able to care for him so far and I pray that I stay healthy enough to keep taking care of him.
items.label: stay healthy enough to keep caregiving

items.quote: It’s hard for me to leave him in someone else’s care even for a few hours because I know his specific needs
items.label: hard to leave him with others

items.quote: when there’s no family restroom and my DH has to go into the men’s room by himself and there’s no other men going on or coming out
items.label: no family restroom when out

items.quote: I think I am an awful person for hoping one of those things happen sooner not later.
items.label: guilt over wanting placement sooner

items.quote: I am ready to move ahead with MC for my DW.
items.label: move wife to memory care

items.quote: In the end for me, it has become primarily an issue of safety for her (out of control anger and agitation, losing balance, close to wandering when angry).
items.label: wife's safety

items.quote: It is a huge decision for us, as what will I have after he’s gone? And living on my income if/when he is in MC will be tight!
items.label: cost of memory care and own future

items.quote: The falls started and I can’t get him up off the floor.
items.label: falls I cannot handle

items.quote: The stress is so overwhelming for me I fear a stroke or heart attack.
items.label: stress threatens my own health

items.quote: I am wondering whether this is something not to bother pointing out, as this tends to provoke a range of emotions, from irritation to anger.
items.label: pointing out mistakes provokes anger

items.quote: I want DH to maintain sense of dignity.
items.label: protect his dignity

items.quote: Sometimes I get frustrated by the re-doing as it is more work than if I had done it in the beginning
items.label: redoing his chores is frustrating

items.quote: As to maintaining and restoring abilities, I continue to aggressively pursue options.
items.label: restore her abilities

items.quote: She needs to be doing something all the time and expects me to provide her with something to do.
items.label: must keep her occupied constantly

items.quote: I couldn't survive without this help but it's not enough.
items.label: daycare is not enough help

items.quote: I am exhausted, constantly crying through frustration and exhaustion.
items.label: exhausted and constantly crying

items.quote: The entertainment and engagement effort is exhausting to me.
items.label: keeping her engaged is exhausting

items.quote: I'm wondering if she would be better off living at a memory care facility where she would.have professional care full-time.
items.label: consider memory care full-time

items.quote: I very selfishly want to have life left to live when this is over.
items.label: have a life left afterward

items.quote: I have so much on my plate as full time caregiver I just can’t do any more.
items.label: too much on my plate

items.quote: my DH has low tolerance for interruptions to his routine… especially after 5 pm or so.
items.label: routine interruptions upset him in evening

items.quote: Recently, she has had some changes that has led her neurologist to suggesting we get a hospice evaluation.
items.label: get a hospice evaluation

items.quote: I am tired of doing it all - cooking, cleaning, daily laundry, paying bills, grocery shoping, doctors appointments, I’m even tired of crying everyday
items.label: doing every task alone

items.quote: those I held near and dear are “ too busy” to lend a hand, give me a call, or ask how I’m doing.
items.label: friends and family offer no help

items.quote: I have got to find a way to cope with the world I’m living in.
items.label: find a way to cope

items.quote: I am now starting to create a new life for me and my remaining time here on earth.
items.label: build a new life for myself

items.quote: it is a daily challenge not to let this disease take me down with my DH.
items.label: not be taken down by the disease

items.quote: I feel like I am losing myself as a caregiver because I don't ever have time to myself to do anything that I want to do?
items.label: time to myself

items.quote: if I leave the room or go outside, he's constantly watching over me
items.label: husband watches me constantly

items.quote: I still love my husband so much, I'd rather have the difficulty of taking care of him than to not have him in my life.
items.label: love, prefers difficulty to losing him

items.quote: someone I can talk to without judgement and willing to work WITH me to help with my severe anxiety and depression.
items.label: therapy for own anxiety and depression

items.quote: the bigger problem for me is his daughter and exwife that have given me more grief than anyone else. They aren't supportive, they degrade me
items.label: unsupportive stepchild and ex-wife

items.quote: I don’t want to dump on my friends or family.
items.label: no one to vent to

items.quote: starting with me getting back to taking my 30 minute walks which I used to do at least 5 times a week.
items.label: get back to my daily walks

items.quote: My expectations of the staff is to ensure my DH is feed, showered, and toileted.
items.label: staff keep him fed, clean, toileted

items.quote: I do not want the staff to have confrontations with him.
items.label: avoid staff conflicts with him

items.quote: She was upset that my DH did not have a polo shirt and jeans on.
items.label: sister-in-law criticizes his clothes

items.quote: pretty much everything has changed and it is non stop on my side and it drains me to know end.
items.label: non-stop, draining care since diagnosis

items.quote: I work full time and it is just me. No family around this area.
items.label: working full time with no family nearby

items.quote: I knew if I quit my job I would be miserable and it would not change the trajectory of the disease.
items.label: keep my job

items.quote: My wife, who has Alzheimer’s, is constantly saying she wants to go home (we are living at home), she doesn’t want to be here anymore, and she can’t do this anymore.
items.label: wife keeps saying she wants to go home

items.quote: I’ve tried telling her she’s safe here, asking her to tell me about home, and other tactics I’ve seen here and elsewhere, to no avail.
items.label: calming tactics are not working

items.quote: I found these conversations very confronting and for most of this time I was in tears, distraught.
items.label: go-home talks leave me distraught

items.quote: The constant criticism, being blamed for everything…it goes on and on.
items.label: constant criticism and blame

items.quote: after I thought about how bad it must be on her to be in such a volatile state and not know why most of the time, I changed my mind.
items.label: compassion for her distress

items.quote: the weekend staffing level is not as good as the weekdays. I have to visit him most days to make sure he is ok.
items.label: must visit nursing home to ensure his care

items.quote: It’s very hard being solely responsible for him.
items.label: solely responsible for him

items.quote: I don’t know how much longer this journey will last.
items.label: uncertain how long this will last

items.quote: There’s something off with some of his cognitive abilities but we do not have a why or what it is.
items.label: no clear diagnosis for his decline

items.quote: I’m a fixer and I can’t fix this.
items.label: cannot fix his condition

items.quote: my question is how to you get someone in to spend time with her so I can leave her alone??
items.label: get someone to stay with wife

items.quote: The fact that I would suggest it would upset her and wouldn’t be happy about it
items.label: she would resist outside help

items.quote: he wouldn't think to call 911 if there was a fire or other emergency
items.label: husband alone could not handle emergency

items.quote: I know I need some help but don't know if I should try the GUIDE PROGRAM and see if he qualifies for VA catastrophic disabity rating of if it's time for a hospice evaluation.
items.label: get help: GUIDE, VA, or hospice

items.quote: Not sure what help to apply for first.
items.label: unsure which help to apply for

items.quote: I am so very thankful I looked into getting help and got the gift of hospice for her sake.
items.label: getting hospice help for her sake

items.quote: my thinking is that we can save money on the insurance and could use that to pay for the visit if necessary.
items.label: save money on dental insurance
